title: Pair mapping with a space bound
statement: Let $g$ be a function from Boolean words to Boolean words, and let $T_g,S_g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be monotone. Suppose a finite Turing machine $M_g$ computes $g$ within time $T_g$, and for every Boolean word $y$ and every time $t\in\mathbb{N}$ its computation on $y$ uses at most $S_g(|y|)$ work-tape cells. Then there are a finite Turing machine $M$ and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean input $z$, $M$ halts within $c(|z|+1+T_g(|z|))$ steps and outputs the pairing of $a$ with $g(b)$ if the aligned pair parser returns $(a,b)$ on $z$, and the empty word if parsing fails. At every time $t\in\mathbb{N}$, the computation of $M$ on $z$ uses at most $S_g(|z|)+c(|z|+1)$ work-tape cells.
